evidence.note: Explicit leaf-first plan: explore structure, build common first, then storage, then api-server 'working upward'; each verified with cargo test -p <crate> — matches the level-5 suggested ordering with compiles+tests-pass milestone check.
Sub-milestone inside the large common crate: 'implement common/src/lib.rs with types module first, then resources module' — a small structure element leaning toward the level-8 anchor.
Sequenced storage then api-server after common compiled, using per-crate cargo build/test — sustained leaf-to-root ordering.

After api-server the plan collapses into workspace-wide undifferentiated error-chasing (224 errors, mass edits to common types to satisfy all crates at once); no gating of downstream layers on prior-layer-green.

Downstream crates (controller-manager, kubelet, etc.) only touched reactively; final plans are repetitive 'add type, rebuild, count passes' to-do lists with no exit criteria or re-ordering by critical path — milestone discipline not sustained to the end.

reasoning: The agent clearly followed the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check, squarely matching the level-5 anchor, and added a small amount of sub-milestone structure inside common (types→resources). However, it did not reach level 8: there was no dependency-aware milestone plan with concrete exit criteria for all ten crates, the six downstream crates never received milestone treatment, and after api-server the work degraded into undifferentiated workspace-wide error-chasing rather than gating each layer on the prior being green. The small sub-milestone element is not enough to push above 5 given the un-sustained plan across the full horizon.
